title: CAIT Kashmir seeks special trade revival package for J&K traders

ai.summary: CAIT Kashmir Chapter President Farhan Kitab called for a Trade Revival Package to address economic disruptions in Jammu and Kashmir, citing business closures, declining purchasing power, and liquidity constraints.

facts.claim: CAIT Kashmir Chapter President Farhan Kitab called for a comprehensive Trade Revival Package for the Union Territory
facts.quote: Representing Jammu and Kashmir, CAIT Kashmir Chapter President Farhan Kitab called for a comprehensive Trade Revival Package for the Union Territory, citing prolonged economic disruptions, business closures, declining purchasing power, liquidity constraints and mounting financial liabilities faced by traders.

facts.claim: citing prolonged economic disruptions, business closures, declining purchasing power, liquidity constraints and mounting financial liabilities faced by traders
facts.quote: citing prolonged economic disruptions, business closures, declining purchasing power, liquidity constraints and mounting financial liabilities faced by traders.

facts.claim: He urged the Government of India and the J&K Government to introduce targeted financial measures to help businesses recover from the sustained economic challenges
facts.quote: He urged the Government of India and the J&K Government to introduce targeted financial measures to help businesses recover from the sustained economic challenges.

facts.claim: Kitab sought interest subvention, affordable working capital, loan restructuring and One-Time Settlement (OTS) facilities, relief in legacy liabilities and enhanced credit support for struggling retailers and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
facts.quote: Kitab sought interest subvention, affordable working capital, loan restructuring and One-Time Settlement (OTS) facilities, relief in legacy liabilities and enhanced credit support for struggling retailers and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

facts.claim: He said repeated disruptions had severely eroded the capital base of Kashmir’s trading community, making it difficult for businesses to sustain operations, meet financial obligations and retain employment
facts.quote: He said repeated disruptions had severely eroded the capital base of Kashmir’s trading community, making it difficult for businesses to sustain operations, meet financial obligations and retain employment.
